newsitem.title: USA: Scottish researcher opposes human cloning.
newsitem.headline: Scottish researcher opposes human cloning.

text.p: The Scottish scientist who cloned a sheep opposed human cloning as he prepared to testify about the emotional issue before the U.S. Senate on Wednesday.

Ian Wilmut, who jolted the world last month by revealing a sheep clone named Dolly, said he had not heard of any morally acceptable reason to clone a human being, but he cautioned against a ban that would be so broadly worded it could rule out related research to treat or prevent human diseases.

"I have not heard any application of this -- to copy a person -- that I think it's appropriate," Wilmut told reporters before testifying at a Senate panel. He declined to say what he thought U.S. lawmakers should do but said he was comfortable with Britain's legal restrictions on human cloning.

Sen. Bill Frist, the Tennessee Republican who will chair the hearing, who was a heart transplant surgeon before entering politics, said he hoped lawmakers would tread carefully to rule out ethically wrong cloning research without jeopardising scientific study of diseases such as breast cancer, cystic fibrosis and sickle cell anaemia.
